title: My Worst Meeting Ever
script: Narrator: [warmly] I want to tell you about the worst meeting of my career, because looking back now, it's actually a little funny.
Narrator: It happened during my second month at a new company, when I still didn't know everyone's name.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I was presenting our quarterly numbers to the whole department, including the company's owner, who rarely attended these meetings.
Narrator: I had practiced my slides the night before, so I felt reasonably confident when I walked into the room that morning.
Narrator: [carefully] Then, halfway through my presentation, my laptop suddenly froze, and the screen showed my personal photos instead of the report.
Narrator: Everyone saw a photo of my cat wearing a tiny hat, right there on the big screen for the whole department.
Narrator: [reflective] My face turned bright red, and for a moment, I genuinely considered running out of the room and never coming back.
Narrator: Instead, I took a breath, closed the photo app, and said, well, at least you know I have excellent taste in hats.
Narrator: [honestly] To my surprise, the room actually laughed, and even the owner smiled, which helped me relax immediately.
Narrator: I finished the presentation. Afterward, I checked what had appeared and confirmed that no client, document, or sensitive personal image had been exposed.
Narrator: [gently] Before that day, I believed a perfect presentation meant a flawless one, without any mistakes whatsoever.
Narrator: Now I value a calm recovery, but humor does not remove a privacy incident. A mistake should also improve the next process.
Narrator: [encouraging] A coworker named Rani, who I barely knew then, came up afterward and said my reaction actually calmed her own nerves for later meetings.
Narrator: Rani later helped me test a safer setup: a work profile, closed personal apps, hidden notification previews, and only the presentation window shared.
Narrator: [sincere] I can laugh about the harmless cat image now, but the real lesson is to recover respectfully, check the impact, and prevent a more serious exposure next time.
